action: Make a decision on health insurance. After five ticks of avoidance and one tick of acknowledging the gap, actually commit to enrolling the family in a mid-tier marketplace plan. The math is brutal but it is also clear: $1,400 a month hurts. A $60,000 hospitalization without coverage destroys the savings runway entirely. Three dependents. Dale is 50 and does physical labor. He cannot carry this risk indefinitely and tell himself it is acceptable. Complete the application on the state marketplace, select a plan, and submit. Expense goes up by approximately $1,400 a month. Savings accumulation drops from roughly $900 a month to a deficit position. But the savings buffer at $51,863 can absorb this while income holds. This is not a comfortable decision. It is the right one.
